text: 2026-10-01 fsLR frame RESOLVED from primary source (Van Essen, Glasser, Dierker, Harwell, Coalson 2012, Cereb Cortex 22:2241, doi:10.1093/cercor/bhr291, Materials and Methods p.2245, user-supplied PDF). Verbatim: 'To create population-average surfaces for the Conte-69 data set, linear volumetric registration between the individual subject and the MNI152_T1_1mm.nii.gz was performed using ... (FLIRT). (This target is the nonlinearly derived template distributed with FSL version 4.1.7.) The resultant affine transform was applied to the FreeSurfer white, pial, and midthickness surfaces before they had been resampled to the fs_LR mesh. The individual-subject midthickness surfaces were averaged separately for the left and right hemispheres.' Conclusions: (a) Target frame is FSL MNI152_T1_1mm, i.e. TemplateFlow MNI152NLin6Asym (its template_description names 'FSL's MNI ICBM 152 non-linear 6th Generation Asymmetric'; res-01 grid is 182x218x182 with origin (-91,-126,-72), matching FSL's). The 09-23 decision 'fsLR frame = MNI152NLin6Asym' is correct. (b) CORRECTION to my earlier note: per-subject alignment was AFFINE (FLIRT), not FNIRT. The asset is an average of 69 affinely aligned native midthickness surfaces. Admit it as MNI152NLin6Asym with tier 'publisher-declared, affine-aligned group average', not as nonlinear template correspondence. Expect residual anatomical mismatch of several mm relative to the template's own anatomy. Mapping 2009c group volumes through the 6Asym->2009c warp is correct frame handling, but cannot remove that residual. (c) The TemplateFlow asset is byte-identical to Conte69 v2 32k midthickness, and its GIFTI comment lists the 69 averaged subject files, consistent with the methods. Remaining caveat: voxel identity of the TemplateFlow 6Asym T1w with FSL 4.1.7 MNI152_T1_1mm.nii.gz was not hash-checked (no local FSL).
